subject: Audit logs: Access/export format & retention (post-demo follow-up)

Subject: Audit logs: Access/export format & retention (post-demo follow-up)

Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for your time on the demo today — really appreciate you walking through FinCo's data governance constraints. Per our conversation, here is a concise recap of the audit/logging items you asked about and the next steps: 

What you asked for:
- A sample export of audit logs showing who accessed which resources and when (read/write/export),
- Field-level detail (timestamp, actor id/email, action, resource, model id, prompt hash or redacted prompt, token counts, requester IP, KMS key id if applicable),
- Export formats (CSV/NDJSON) and example schema,
- Default retention windows for hosted vs. dedicated/private deployments and options for extended retention or on-demand historical exports,
- Clarification on whether full prompt text is stored and how PII is handled / redacted in logs.

What I’m sharing now:
- Attached: audit_log_schema.csv (column list + short descriptions) and an example NDJSON export (sanitized) we can use as a template.
- Short answers up front: logs can be exported as CSV or NDJSON; default hosted retention is 90 days for detailed prompts by default (we can configure prompt masking/hashing), Dedicated and Private deployments support configurable retention policies (customers can set retention up to multi-year with Dedicated or on-prem), and we can produce on-request historic exports subject to the hosting tier and SLA.

Next steps / asks from FinCo:
1) Confirm whether you need full prompt text in logs, or whether a prompt-hash / redacted prompt is acceptable for auditing.
2) Confirm the retention window you require for audit logs (90 days, 1 year, 7 years, etc.) and whether exports must be delivered to an S3 destination.
3) Any required format (CSV vs NDJSON) or schema changes so we can produce a tailored sample.

If helpful I can loop in Marissa (security & compliance) and Ben (product security) to prepare an evidence package (SOC 2 summaries, export samples) and a short runbook showing how FinCo can request an export.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher

Sean —

Thanks for the clear recap and the sample attachments. Quick clarifications from our side: 
- For regulatory purposes we need proof of who accessed any record containing PII and if any export occurred. Full prompt text would be ideal for now, but if redaction is required we need a reversible method (e.g., deterministic hashing with a customer key) or a documented redaction policy.
- Retention requirement: we are assessing options; baseline is 7 years for audit artifacts but we understand hosted limitations. Can you confirm whether Redwood hosted can commit to producing a 7-year historical export on request, or if that's only possible for Dedicated/Private?
- Format: NDJSON is preferred for ingestion into our SIEM, but we can accept CSV if some fields are nested.

Also: please include SOC 2 evidence and a short description of the encryption/KMS usage for logs.

Appreciate it —
Aisha Rahman
Director, InfoSec — FinCoBank
aisha.rahman@fincobank.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit logs: Access/export format & retention (post-demo follow-up)

Aisha —

Thanks — great questions. Quick responses below and then Marissa/Ben can follow up with the formal evidence package.

Prompt text / PII:
- Hosted (Redwood cloud): by default we retain request metadata and a hashed prompt (deterministic salted hash) for 90 days. Full prompt text is stored for up to 90 days in the default tier unless the customer opts into prompt-redaction. We can support deterministic hashing using a customer-provided salt in Hosted for compliance review (so you can correlate hashes if needed).
- Dedicated/Private: customers can enable full prompt retention and set the retention window via policy; Private deployments (customer-managed network) allow you to control storage and retention entirely.

Historical exports & retention:
- Hosted: standard retention for full prompt text is 90 days. We provide on-request historical exports up to 2 years for customers who have a data-retention add-on or by agreement. For 7-year retention we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment where retention policy can be configured and storage can be provisioned per your needs.

Export format & schema:
- NDJSON export contains one event per line with fields: timestamp, actor_email, actor_id, action, resource_id, model_id, prompt_hash, prompt_redacted (optional), token_count_in, token_count_out, requester_ip, kms_key_id, request_id. 
- We can shift prompt_redacted to be a separate field or include a reversible encryption placeholder if you prefer. Attached is a sanitized NDJSON sample.

Encryption / KMS:
- For Hosted we encrypt logs at rest using AES-256 and manage keys in our KMS; we can provide an evidence report enumerating key rotation and access controls. Dedicated/Private supports customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) for both runtime artifacts and stored logs.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa/Ben to send SOC2 summary + evidence and the S3 export sample by EOD tomorrow (I’m cc’d them).
2) Aisha / FinCo to confirm whether deterministic prompt hashing with customer salt is acceptable as interim, and whether a Dedicated/Private engagement is of interest for multi-year retention.

If you want a short run-through with our security team and an export demo into your SIEM, we can schedule a 30-min call this week.

Best,
Sean

Attachments:
